Tone: cautiously hawkish. The statement highlights strengthening activity and a tight labor market, paired with elevated inflation and heightened uncertainty from the Russia–Ukraine war. The planned path of “ongoing increases” in the policy rate and balance sheet reduction underscores the priority on restoring price stability.

FSR lens: The Financial Stability Report points to lingering vulnerabilities—funding risks in money market and bond funds, potential strains in Treasury market liquidity (as seen in March 2020), and elevated geopolitical/cyber tail risks—that could amplify the growth downside from tighter financial conditions. At the same time, bank capital/liquidity remain solid and household balance sheets are generally stronger than early-pandemic levels, offering some resilience. On net, these FSR insights temper the positive labor backdrop and nudge the tone closer to neutral.
